page: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores clocked at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. With 105 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 with VNNI, it is architected for extreme memory density, provisioning 5,700 GB of RAM, which equates to 27.4 GB per core. Local storage is provided through a 4,398 GB SSD. The configuration includes zero discrete GPUs and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate an intentional tradeoff between single-thread frequency and extreme parallel scale. Single-threaded metrics are constrained, with Geekbench single-core at 1,117.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,371.29, both falling in the bottom 25% of tested systems. In contrast, multi-core capacity ranks in the top 10%, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 187,912.86 and 596.36 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory subsystem performance is strong, registering 10,453.04 GB/sec on cached small-block reads, 359.81 GB/sec on large uncached reads, and driving 149.33 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance consolidates massive memory footprints into a single host, trading per-core single-thread responsiveness for immense total throughput and memory capacity. This design avoids the distributed latency of multi-node clusters for workloads requiring shared memory spaces. It is suited for large enterprise in-memory database engines like SAP HANA, very large Redis caching clusters, high-volume transactional databases, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it couples 5,700 GB of system memory—equating to 27.4 GB per core—with a 4,398 GB local SSD. It includes no hardware GPUs. Performance metrics demonstrate a specialized profile: single-core benchmarks sit in the bottom quartile, but aggregate parallel throughput reaches top-tier levels, demonstrated by 187,912.86 in multi-core stress-ng, top-tier PassMark extended instruction handling, and 149.33 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 10,453.04 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 359.81 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads. The instance prioritizes extreme memory footprint and multi-threaded scaling over single-threaded speed, making it well fitted for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis tiers, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
